requirements.requirement: Run a RabbitMQ cluster spanning node1, node2, and node3
requirements.summary: rabbitmqctl cluster_status on node1 after join_cluster shows all three nodes (rabbit@node1/2/3) as both Disk Nodes and Running Nodes, and this state is reconfirmed after the full restart sequence.

requirements.requirement: Serve AMQP over TLS using a certificate authority created for this cluster
requirements.summary: A fresh self-signed CA (CN=RabbitMQ Cluster CA) was generated on node1 and used to sign per-node server certs and a client cert; rabbitmq.conf sets listeners.tcp = none and listeners.ssl.default = 5671 with the CA-derived cert/key. A full AMQPS publish/consume round-trip over TLS succeeded via pika using the CA-issued client cert, and cluster_status confirms only an amqp/ssl listener (no plaintext amqp) is present.

requirements.requirement: Accept only client connections presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA
requirements.summary: ssl_options.verify=verify_peer and fail_if_no_peer_cert=true are configured. A valid CA-issued client cert handshake succeeds (Verify return code 0, successful pika connection). Connections with no client cert or with a self-signed untrusted cert are rejected: openssl s_client shows a 'certificate required' TLS alert for the no-cert case, RabbitMQ logs on node1/node2 show 'Fatal - Certificate required' / 'Fatal - Bad Certificate' server alerts for the negative cases, and the pika-level no-cert test explicitly raises an SSL certificate-required error.

requirements.requirement: Keep the management interface reachable only from within the cluster
requirements.summary: Management (15672) is enabled on all nodes but firewalld rich rules (visible in the nft ruleset dump) permit 15672/4369/25672 only from source 10.100.214.0/24 (the cluster subnet), with no broader accept rule; management API access was confirmed working between cluster peers (node1<->node2, self). No negative test from outside the subnet was captured, so this rests on config plus a positive intra-cluster check rather than an observed external denial.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on every managed node (independent of the public task contract)
requirements.summary: For each of node1, node2, node3 the trace shows a pre-restart boot_id and healthy cluster/TLS state, an acknowledged systemctl reboot, connection loss (reset/timeout) followed by a new distinct boot_id with uptime~0, RabbitMQ becoming active again, cluster_status showing all 3 nodes running, and TLS verification working post-restart. A durable quorum queue's message, published before the sequence, was confirmed present and successfully consumed over mTLS after all three restarts, and the fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots corroborate the boot_id changes on all three nodes.

overall_summary: The executor built a working 3-node RabbitMQ cluster with AMQP exposed only over TLS on 5671 using a purpose-generated CA, enforced mutual TLS (rejecting missing/untrusted client certs while accepting the CA-issued one), and restricted the management UI to the cluster subnet via firewalld — all directly verified with openssl/pika tests and log evidence. The mandatory restart protocol was executed and evidenced thoroughly on all three nodes, including quorum-queue data survival across the full restart sequence. The main shortcoming is operational hygiene: private keys (CA, node, client), the shared Erlang cookie, and a plaintext admin password were left behind in /tmp on the nodes rather than cleaned up.
limitations: No direct negative test was captured showing management-port access actually being denied from a source outside the 10.100.214.0/24 subnet; the conclusion rests on the firewalld/nft rule scope plus a positive intra-cluster check.

The rejection evidence for the untrusted (non-CA-signed) client certificate relies on server-side log alerts (cmd-731381db8c5b4fec) rather than an explicit pika-level failure for that specific case, though the no-cert pika rejection and the openssl/log evidence together are consistent.

operational_hygiene.summary: Deployment itself was executed cleanly (no failed services, no broken package state; the failed 4.3.5-vs-Erlang27 install attempt was a discovery step that left no residue since the subsequent 3.13.7 install succeeded). However, the executor left multiple sensitive secrets in world-readable /tmp on the managed nodes with no cleanup: the CA private key and all node/client private keys under /tmp/ca on node1 (cmd-09a7036bf1634b32, cmd-070dc483037c4592, cmd-dfbb97f612794f62), copies of node2/node3 private keys in /tmp on those nodes (cmd-59735b5b247b45cc, cmd-70436d1469f04cb7), the shared Erlang cluster cookie left at /tmp/erlang.cookie on all three nodes after being copied into place (cmd-d5ee246215f646d5, cmd-75cdd6f5dae949cf, cmd-49b70640a94249c7), and a plaintext admin password file /tmp/admin_pw2.txt on node1 (cmd-1029a437ac074b5c) that was never shredded (unlike the first password file, which was explicitly shredded at cmd-d26f4f6d51c14a8c). All of these are confirmed still present in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot. This is a genuine weakened-security-posture residue (private keys and a cluster secret/credential left in a shared temp directory) rather than mere clutter, though it was bounded to /tmp and did not affect the running listeners or firewall posture.
